in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

I can see that Alex is 8 years old and doesn't currently live with you. To properly assess your eligibility, I need to understand your circumstances a bit better.

**Key question:** Are you contributing financially to Alex's upkeep, and if so, how much do you contribute?

According to the Child Benefit rules, you can still qualify for Child Benefit for a child who doesn't live with you if you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them - for example on food, clothes or pocket money.

Additionally, when a child goes to live with someone else, you'll usually continue to get Child Benefit for 8 weeks if nobody else claims. After that, it can continue for longer if you make contributions to your child's upkeep that are equal to or more than the Child Benefit payment amount.

Could you tell me:
1. Are you currently making any financial contributions towards Alex's care (such as money for food, clothes, pocket money, or other expenses)?
2. If yes, approximately how much do you contribute per week or month?
3. Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

This information will help me give you an accurate assessment of your eligibility.

I'm sorry, but based on your circumstances, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

While Alex is 8 years old (which meets the age requirement of being under 16), and you live in the UK, the key issue is that you don't meet the "responsibility" criteria for Child Benefit.

To be considered responsible for a child under Child Benefit rules, you must either:
1. **Live with the child**, OR
2. **Pay at least the same amount as Child Benefit** (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them - for example on food, clothes or pocket money

Since Alex doesn't live with you and you're not making any financial contributions towards their upkeep, you don't qualify as being responsible for Alex under these rules.

**What if circumstances change?**
If you start making regular financial contributions towards Alex's care that are equal to or greater than the Child Benefit payment amount, you may become eligible at that point. You would need to contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss your situation if your circumstances change.

If you have any other questions about Child Benefit or need clarification, please feel free to ask.
